newsitem.title: UK: UK parliament likely to vote on handguns on Nov 18.
newsitem.headline: UK parliament likely to vote on handguns on Nov 18.

text.p: British members of parliament are likely to vote on November 18 on whether to impose a complete ban on private ownership of handguns in the aftermath of the Dunblane tragedy, ministerial sources said on Thursday.
Earlier, leader of the House of Commons Tony Newton announced that the second reading of the Firearms (Amendment) Bill which proposes changes in the rules on handguns will be considered next Tuesday.

The sources said after the expected passage of the second reading, MPs will be invited to vote on a procedural motion under which certain controversial clauses of the bill would be dealt with by a Committee consisting of all MPs.
This Committee will meet on November 18 to discuss the government proposal to ban all handguns except for .22 calibre weapons used in target shooting.
The sources said they expected that a vote on an opposition amendment for a complete ban on the weapons would be debated then.
